title: Genome-wide identification of the GRAS gene family and evidence for the involvement of PgGRAS48 in main root development in Panax ginseng.
authors: Wang, Yihan; Wang, Ping; Di, Peng; Wang, Yingping
one_liner_zh: 该文对人参GRAS转录因子家族进行全基因组鉴定，并实验验证PgGRAS48与DELLA互作调控主根发育，虽涉及TF-DNA互作但缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，仅用分子对接辅助，深度不足。
abstract: Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer (ginseng) is one of the most widely used traditional Chinese medicinal herbs, with its roots as the primary medicinal part garnering significant attention due to their therapeutic potential. The GRAS [GRI (Gibberellic Acid Insensitive), RGA (Repressor of GAI-3 mutant), and SCR (Scarecrow)] genes are a class of widely distributed plant-specific transcription factors that play crucial roles in various physiological processes including root formation, fruit development, hormone signaling, and stem cell maintenance. This study systematically identified 139 GRAS genes (PgGRAS) in the ginseng genome for the first time, analyzing their complexity and diversity through protein domain structure, phylogenetic relationships, gene structure, and cis-acting element prediction. Evolutionary analysis revealed that all PgGRAS members were divided into 14 evolutionary branches, including a novel species-specific subfamily PG28, with segmental duplication being the primary driver of family expansion. RNA-seq analysis uncovered tissue-specific expression patterns of the PgGRAS gene family. qRT-PCR validation demonstrated that PgGRAS48, a member of the SCL3 subfamily, was significantly highly expressed in the main root and upregulated upon GA treatment, suggesting its potential regulatory role in main root development. Therefore, this gene was selected for further investigation. Overexpression of PgGRAS48 significantly increased the main root length in Arabidopsis thaliana (A. thaliana), accompanied by elevated endogenous GA levels. Subcellular localization, molecular docking, Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation (BIFC) and yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) experiments confirmed the interaction between PgGRAS48 (SCL3) and PgGRAS2 (DELLA) in the nucleus, revealing the molecular mechanism by which SCL3-DELLA regulates main root elongation through gibberellin (GA) biosynthesis or signaling pathways. This study elucidates the molecular network of the GRAS family in root development in ginseng, providing key targets for the targeted improvement of root architecture in medicinal plants.
abstract_zh: 人参（Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer）是最广泛使用的传统中草药之一，其根部作为主要药用部分因其治疗潜力而受到显著关注。GRAS [GRI (Gibberellic Acid Insensitive)、RGA (Repressor of GAI-3 mutant) 和 SCR (Scarecrow)] 基因是一类广泛分布的植物特异性转录因子，在根形成、果实发育、激素信号传导和干细胞维持等多种生理过程中发挥关键作用。本研究首次系统鉴定了人参基因组中的139个GRAS基因（PgGRAS），通过蛋白质结构域、系统发育关系、基因结构和顺式作用元件预测分析了其复杂性和多样性。进化分析显示，所有PgGRAS成员被分为14个进化分支，包括一个新颖的物种特异性亚家族PG28，其中片段重复是家族扩张的主要驱动力。RNA-seq分析揭示了PgGRAS基因家族的组织特异性表达模式。qRT-PCR验证表明，SCL3亚家族成员PgGRAS48在主根中显著高表达，并在GA处理后上调，提示其在主根发育中可能具有调控作用。因此，该基因被选作进一步研究。PgGRAS48的过表达显著增加了拟南芥（A. thaliana）的主根长度，并伴随内源GA水平升高。亚细胞定位、分子对接、双分子荧光互补（BIFC）和酵母双杂交（Y2H）实验证实了PgGRAS48（SCL3）与PgGRAS2（DELLA）在细胞核中的相互作用，揭示了SCL3-DELLA通过赤霉素（GA）生物合成或信号通路调控主根伸长的分子机制。本研究阐明了人参中GRAS家族在根发育中的分子网络，为药用植物根结构的定向改良提供了关键靶点。
